speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you tell me exactly how your leg was positioned when the accident happened and if you heard a loud pop at the time?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bilateral Posterior Cruciate Ligament (PCL) injuries with a likely associated Right Anterior Cruciate Ligament (ACL) injury and/or Right Femoral Neck fracture.

The mechanism (rear-end collision with restrained driver) and immediate onset of bilateral knee pain combined with severe right groin pain is highly suspicious for high-energy knee ligamentous disruption and potential hip pathology. Given the "abnormal leg positioning" you mentioned, I need to confirm if you currently have any deformity of the right hip or leg, and whether you can actively bear weight on the right leg at all. REQUEST TEST: Right Hip X-Ray (AP and Lateral views).
